title: performance(canary): adaptive hysteresis and sensitivity tuning for auto-detection rollout guards
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We've seen intermittent small regressions flagged too aggressively by the perf canary when traffic variance is high; this leads to unnecessary rollbacks and developer fatigue. This PR implements an adaptive hysteresis and sensitivity tuning layer for the performance-canary detector so that small, transient blips do not trigger automated rollout guards while still preserving fast detection of true regressions. Summary: 1) Add adaptive hysteresis windowing based on traffic variance and recent false-positive rate; 2) Introduce sensitivity profiles (low/medium/high) with automatic selection driven by workload signal (p50/p90 p99 stability); 3) Add a short-term KV cache of observed baseline metrics to avoid repeated alerts for warming noise; 4) Instrument canary evaluation controller with additional debug metrics and tracing; 5) Expose new rollout_guard config knobs via the API and console for SREs and platform owners. Checklist: - [x] Design doc approved (ENG-3291) - [x] Unit tests for detector math - [x] Integration tests with perf-canary lab harness - [x] E2E smoke in staging with synthetic high-variance traffic - [x] Docs + console release notes updated - [x] SRE signoff on safe defaults Implementation notes: Detector now computes an adaptive threshold that scales with observed standard deviation over a configurable lookback, combined with a hysteresis counter that requires N consecutive windows over threshold before triggering an action. Sensitivity profiles adjust the multiplier and minimum detection windows: low (conservative), medium (default), high (aggressive). Default remains medium to avoid breaking existing customers. Metrics added: canary.adaptive_threshold, canary.hysteresis_count, canary.false_positive_rate_est, canary.sensitivity_profile. Rollout guard behavior: when the canary detector fires, the controller will only mark the rollout as blocked after hysteresis_count >= profile.min_consecutive and the adaptive_threshold exceedance persists; automatic rollback remains unchanged but now waits an extra stabilization window when traffic variance is high. Backwards compatibility: new config fields are optional with sensible defaults to preserve current behavior. Testing: Ran bench harness with 10K synthetic requests/min across 12-hour runs reproducing both stable and high-variance patterns. False positive rate dropped from ~6.1% to ~0.8% in high-variance traces while time-to-detect real 10% p90 regressions remained within target (<=90s). Follow-ups: - Consider adding per-model sensitivity tuning using historical evals - Expose a REST endpoint to query current sensitivity profile per-route
